article.body:
chayolim just like you. Welcome to our podcast, where

Chayolim, in what way can this week’s lesson make a difference to you? What changes can you make in your own life?

But … don’t let it stop here! Conduct your own interviews at the Shabbos table. Choose someone

to be the podcast’s guest, and together explore how to live with the messages from the parsha.

Mimi, you’re playing that niggun beautifully, but can you please take a break so we can record our podcast?

But I really need to keep practicing. Violin is super difficult and if I don’t practice for enough hours a day, I’ll never perfect my technique! Can’t you just do the podcast without me?

No way, Mimi! Besides, you’re obsessed with that violin. You literally practice all day long! Mommy has to call you like a million times for dinner.

Can you all please just leave me alone for a few minutes?

That’s it. I’m going to call our guest. Maybe that’ll snap you out of this.

Ah, shalom! You have reached Lior’s wax studio. How can I help you today?

Wait, you have a studio? Like a real artist? That is so impressive.

Thank you, thank you. I like to make wax sculptures. I make all sorts of different shapes—fruits, instruments, people—and for this week's parsha, I am making a menorah.

How did you learn this craft? I want to become an artist, too!

You know, I used to spend all day locked up in my studio. I love modeling, and all I wanted to do was improve my skill. Eating and sleeping were a waste of time. I was 100% focused on my wax.

I totally get you! I would spend all day with my violin if my siblings weren’t always pulling me away from it.

Ah! But you are forgetting something important. It says in Mishlei, “ֵנֵר ה’ ִנְִׁשְַמַת ָאָָדָם - the neshama of a Yid is Hashem’s candle.” Tell me, who lit the candles in the menorah of the Bais Hamikdash?

Yes! Now let me tell you about the menorah’s flames: Fire usually reaches upwards, but these flames all faced the middle branch. As it says in this week’s parsha, “ְעַת ה ַנֵרֹות אֶל מּול פְּנֵי הַמְנֹורָה יָאִירּו שִׁב”.

Well, do you know what the middle of the menorah represents?

Hashem! Wait, I think I get it. We are the candles, and Hashem is in the center. We learn from the menorah to make Hashem the center of our lives.

Exactly! Now I want you all to do something. Close your eyes for a moment and think about your neshama and of making Hashem the center.

Good question. I'll answer that with another passuk from Mishlei: “ֵנֵר ִמְִצְָוָה ְוְתֹוָר ָה אֹור—a mitzvah is a candle, and Torah is light.”

But what happened to your obsession? I mean you still make sculptures; does that mean that Hashem isn't your focus?

Basya, to me, Reb Lior looks like a great role model for us. He uses his talents and passions, but keeps Hashem as the top priority. The candles he creates are there to add beauty to mitzvos.

Thank you. I do try! It wasn't always this way, but now I make time to eat, sleep, and learn Torah. I know that I need ko’ach to serve Hashem.
